title: kv-cache: adaptive spillover eviction and memory defrag heuristics (v37)
author: Priya Raman
description: Context: production KV cache under mixed OLTP/long-context workloads showed increased fragmentation and aggressive spillover during sudden short-sequence spikes. This caused higher tail latency and increased disk I/O in private deployments with constrained GPU memory. Motivation: previous heuristics (v36) reduced average spillover but left pathological fragmentation patterns for interleaved short/long requests. This PR introduces an adaptive eviction scoring function and a cooperative background defragmentation/compaction scheduler that targets spillover-prone shards and reduces paging churn. Goals: 1) reduce 95/99p latency regressions caused by spillover churn, 2) lower aggregated spillover I/O, 3) keep foreground latency SLOs intact.
summary_of_changes:
- New adaptive eviction scorer (weighting recency, token-span, fragmentation score, and spillover-risk estimate)
- Background compactor that performs prioritized in-place compaction with low-priority IO and time-sliced CPU to avoid blocking inference threads
- Spillover watermarks and hysteresis: conservative -> aggressive thresholds to avoid oscillation
- Cooperative scheduling: compactor yields to continuous-batching hot paths and respects runtime scheduling priorities
- Config knobs: runtime.kv.eviction.strategy=adaptive, runtime.kv.compactor.max_cpu_pct, runtime.kv.spill.watermarks, runtime.kv.defrag.batch_ms
- Instrumentation: new metrics (kv.compactor.seconds_run, kv.eviction.score_distribution, kv.spill.io_bytes, kv.fragmentation_ratio) and dashboards updated
- Unit and integration tests for corner cases (interleaved short/long sequences, rapid ramp up, compactor preemption)

changed_snippets:
runtime/kv_cache/eviction_scorer.rs: new function compute_adaptive_score(node) uses recency_score*0.4 + span_score*0.3 + frag_penalty*0.2 + spill_risk*0.1
runtime/kv_cache/compactor.rs: compactor runs as low-priority task, uses time-sliced passes (default 50ms) and yields on runtime.is_busy()
config: default policy set to 'adaptive' for newly created pools
benchmark_results: Microbench (internal bench): -95p latency reduced from 210ms -> 185ms (12% improvement) on mixed short/long workload; Spill IOPS down 28%; Aggregate token throughput unchanged. Perf lab: no regression on large-context workloads; slight CPU increase (avg +3%) due to compaction background work; tunable via runtime.kv.compactor.max_cpu_pct.
